definitions.explanation: The large Arctic sea mammal with long tusks and whiskers. Usually written in katakana; the kanji spelling is {海象|せいうち}.

examples.japanese: セイウチ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{牙|きば}→牙：16154_kiba⟧。

examples.english: A walrus is sleeping on the ice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{水族館|すいぞくかん}→水族館：09220_suizokukan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧セイウチ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{飼育員|しいくいん}→飼育員：17861_shiikuin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{合図|あいず}→合図：01675_aizu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}して→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦{観客|かんきゃく}→観客：02556_kankyaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{笑|わら}わせた→笑う：00685_warau⟧。
examples.english: At the aquarium, the walrus made a loud noise on the keeper's cue and made the audience laugh.

notes:
The word is said to come from Russian. Walruses, seals and sea lions are often confused; the walrus is the one with tusks.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦アザラシ→アザラシ：06561_azarashi⟧: seal (no ear flaps, no tusks)
- ⟦アシカ→アシカ：29995_ashika⟧: sea lion (ear flaps, walks on its flippers)
- トド: Steller sea lion
